A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRUNE research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original sequential-editing experiments, downstream evaluations, singular-value measurements and supplementary analyses in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds ConceptEdit experiments and a comparison of single versus repeated PRUNE application.

M1.justification: The SVD-based restraint and Equations 3–6 remain unchanged. V2 adds an evaluated variant applying PRUNE repeatedly during editing in Appendix C.6; v1 applies it after editing and mentions repeated application only as future work.

E1.justification: V2 adds conceptual-knowledge editing using ConceptEdit, including concept-instance relationships, substantially extending evaluation beyond factual triples. CounterFact, ZSRE and the four downstream tasks remain; their relocation does not constitute added coverage.

E2.justification: The baseline editors remain MEND, ROME and MEMIT, with the same model-specific availability. ConceptEdit uses the existing ROME comparator, while Appendix C.6 compares PRUNE application variants. Newly cited editing methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: New protocols include ConceptEdit's Instance Change metric and single-versus-repeated PRUNE evaluation at 100 and 500 edits. Figure 5 changes its stated model from LLaMA-3 (8B) to LLaMA-2 (7B), although its points are unchanged. The factual-dataset metric definitions are retained across main-text/appendix moves.

E4.justification: Appendix C.6 adds a targeted ablation testing whether repeated PRUNE application improves longer-term retention. Appendix C.5 jointly examines condition-number and downstream-performance trajectories. The earlier linear-versus-log restraint analysis and forgetting analysis remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report t-tests with p-value below 0.05 for the main performance comparisons. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or another uncertainty-estimation procedure; the new correlation plot does not report a correlation statistic.

E6.justification: V2 adds ConceptEdit results in Table 2 and repeated-application results in Table 6. The latter reports 84.6% versus 56.80% efficacy for repeated versus single PRUNE application after 500 GPT-2 XL/ROME CounterFact edits. Existing ZSRE MEND+PRUNE reasoning and open-QA results at 15 edits also change between v1 Figure 8 and v2 Figure 3.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1–3.2 and Appendix A's definitions, lemmas, bounds and proofs are retained. Section 4's added repeated-update example provides intuitive motivation rather than a new theoretical result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims that escalating condition numbers explain sequential-editing degradation and that PRUNE preserves general abilities while maintaining editing performance. The additional experiments support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4 expands the explanation of editing overfitting through coordinated updates. Section 5.6 adds a substantive limitation: changing conceptual definitions can leave instance relationships unchanged. The factual-only and single-application future-work statements are removed following the corresponding new experiments.

D1.justification: V1 explicitly advertises code and data; v2's footnote mentions only code at the same repository. This narrows the disclosure without establishing that data were withdrawn. Existing software, hyperparameter, prompt and hardware details remain; the new repetition schedule and ConceptEdit hyperparameters are unspecified.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Rebuilding ROME, A Unified Framework for Model Editing and The Butterfly Effect of Model Editing, while removing the Cheng and Gong quantization references. The main positioning relative to previous editing research remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 expands explanations in Sections 3.3–4, centers the experimental narrative on ZSRE, inserts a conceptual-editing subsection, integrates limitations into the conclusion and adds acknowledgments. Most existing prose and the overall section organization remain.

P2.justification: V2 adds a ConceptEdit example, two results tables and a joint condition-number/performance plot. ZSRE plots move into the main text while corresponding CounterFact plots move to the appendix. ICLR headers and typography change, but existing plot and table designs are largely retained.

improvement.justification: ConceptEdit results and the repeated-application comparison provide evidence for two directions left untested in v1, while exposing a useful limitation concerning concept-instance consistency. These strengthen empirical scope and practical understanding. The gains remain limited by unspecified settings for the new experiments and the unexplained Figure 5 model relabeling; the core theory and claims are unchanged.
